title: Entity resolution and alias graph
description: Resolve signals to canonical entities — identity, host, IP, session, mailbox — maintaining aliases so a user's UPN, object id and email are recognised as one entity.
acceptance: Identity aliases (UPN, object id, primary and proxy addresses) resolve to one canonical entity
Resolution is tenant-scoped; identical identifiers in different tenants never merge
Unresolvable entities are retained as provisional rather than discarded
Resolution adds under 5 milliseconds p99 to signal processing
An alias merge is reversible and audited, because a bad merge corrupts correlation

tests.desc: UPN, object id and email for one user resolve to a single entity
Identical email addresses in two tenants resolve to two distinct entities
An unknown identifier produces a provisional entity rather than an error
An alias merge can be reversed and the reversal is audited

title: Signal clustering into cases
description: The component that makes the product viable. Signals sharing an entity within a sliding window become one case. Contains no AI.
acceptance: Default 60-minute sliding window with per-rule override
Signals sharing any entity within the window join the same case
A late-arriving signal joins an open case rather than creating a duplicate
A case closes its window after a configurable quiet period
Clustering is deterministic — identical input produces an identical case set

tests.desc: Three signals on one identity within the window produce one case
Signals on one identity outside the window produce two cases
A signal arriving late joins the existing open case
Replaying identical input twice produces an identical case set
The brief's BEC scenario — impossible travel then inbox rule — produces exactly one case

title: Case lifecycle and append-only transition log
description: States open, triaging, investigating, awaiting_approval, actioned, closed, dismissed — with every transition appended, never overwritten, so a case's full history is reconstructible.
acceptance: Transitions are appended; current state is derived, never stored destructively
Illegal transitions are rejected with a clear error
Every transition records actor type, actor id, timestamp and reason
A case's full history is reconstructible from the log alone
Transition events are written in the same transaction as the audit entry

tests.desc: Every legal transition is permitted and every illegal one is rejected
Case state is correctly derived from an arbitrary transition sequence
A transition and its audit entry commit atomically or not at all
Full case history is reconstructible after 100 transitions

title: Case scoring and escalation threshold
description: Score cases deterministically before any LLM sees them, so the expensive model is spent only where it is earned.
acceptance: Score combines entity criticality, signal count, maximum severity, MITRE kill-chain progression and baseline deviation
A case spanning two kill-chain stages outranks two single-stage cases
The escalation threshold is configurable per tenant plan tier
Score components are stored so a score is explainable after the fact
Scoring is pure and deterministic

tests.desc: A multi-stage kill-chain case scores above a single-stage case with the same signal count
A case touching a flagged high-value identity scores above an equivalent case on an ordinary identity
Scoring is deterministic across repeated invocations
Stored score components reproduce the final score exactly

title: Entity baselines for anomaly context
description: Per-entity behavioural baselines — usual countries, devices, sign-in hours, typical data volumes — computed in ClickHouse and used by scoring and by the AI analyst as a tool.
acceptance: Baselines cover usual countries, ASNs, devices, sign-in hour distribution and data-transfer volume
A rolling 30-day window with a minimum-observation threshold before a baseline is considered valid
A new entity with insufficient history is explicitly marked as such, never treated as anomalous by default
Baselines are exposed as a tool the analyst can call
Recomputation is incremental, not a full rescan

tests.desc: Baseline correctly identifies a habitual sign-in country from seeded history
An entity below the observation threshold returns insufficient-data rather than a baseline
Incremental recomputation matches a full recomputation
A new employee's first week does not generate anomaly signals purely from novelty

title: Reduction-ratio SLO instrumentation
description: The 10:1 signal-to-case reduction is a business-critical SLO, not an aspiration. Measure it per tenant per day and alert when it degrades.
acceptance: signals_in / cases_escalated is computed and exported per tenant per day
An alert fires when the ratio drops below 8:1
The platform-wide ratio is visible on the operations dashboard
The metric is backfillable from historical data for trend analysis
Degradation is documented as a product incident, with a runbook

tests.desc: Ratio is computed correctly from a seeded signal and case set
A deliberately noisy rule drives the ratio below threshold and fires the alert
A tenant with zero signals produces no division error and no spurious alert

title: Dismissed-signal digest
description: Implements the 'nothing is hidden' guarantee. Every signal that did not escalate is retained and summarised daily with the reason it was closed.
acceptance: Every non-escalated signal records a machine-readable dismissal reason
A daily digest per tenant lists dismissals grouped by reason
The digest is retrievable through the API and rendered in the dashboard
No signal is ever deleted rather than dismissed
A dismissal can be challenged, which reopens the case and is audited

tests.desc: Every dismissed signal appears in that day's digest
A dismissal without a reason is rejected at write time
Challenging a dismissal reopens the case and writes an audit entry

title: Case contract freeze in the shared schema
description: Freeze the Case contract so dashboard work can parallelise from here, as the roadmap dependency graph requires.
acceptance: The Case contract is finalised in packages/schema and versioned
A compatibility policy is documented: additive changes only without a major version bump
Both the Go and TypeScript generated types are published
A CI check fails on a breaking change without a version bump
The frozen contract is announced in the roadmap as the parallelisation gate

tests.desc: A breaking change without a version bump fails the compatibility check
An additive field change passes
Go and TypeScript consumers both compile against the frozen contract

title: Correlation replay harness for ratio measurement
description: The P3 exit criterion as an executable test: replay a realistic week of data and measure the actual reduction ratio.
acceptance: Replays a seeded realistic dataset containing both benign noise and a known attack sequence
Measures and reports the reduction ratio
Asserts the known attack produces exactly one escalated case
Asserts the ratio is at least 10:1
Runs in CI on a reduced dataset and nightly on the full one

tests.desc: Reduction ratio on the reference dataset is at least 10:1
The seeded attack sequence yields exactly one escalated case
No benign pattern in the reference set escalates

title: Hot-tenant correlation sharding readiness
description: Ensure correlation can merge windows across the shard suffix introduced in P1-05, so the Phase 7 hot-tenant split is a configuration change rather than a redesign.
acceptance: Correlation reads the shard suffix and merges windows for a sharded tenant
Merging is correct when a tenant's signals span multiple shards
Behaviour is identical for an unsharded tenant
The merge path is tested even though sharding is not yet enabled in production

tests.desc: Signals across two shards for one tenant cluster into one case
An unsharded tenant behaves identically to before
Enabling sharding mid-stream does not split an open case
